content:
We have carbon NMR shifts list. Aromatic carbons typically appear ~110-160 ppm. The list includes many values: 160.80, 135.43, 130.70, 130.40, 128.70, 128.35, 124.85, then aliphatic: 57.20, 41.00, 39.20, 34.00, 24.56, 19.40, 16.60.

So aromatic carbons likely those in 110-160 region: we have 7 values (160.80, 135.43, 130.70, 130.40, 128.70, 128.35, 124.85). That's 7 aromatic carbons.

But need to consider if any of those could be non-aromatic (e.g., carbonyl at 160.80 maybe a C=O). 160.8 could be a carbonyl (e.g., ester, amide). However aromatic carbons also can be around 160 for phenyl attached to electron-withdrawing groups (e.g., phenyl carbon attached to O). But typical aromatic carbon attached to heteroatom can be ~150-160. So ambiguous.

We could get HSQC to assign but cost. However we can also retrieve typical carbon shift ranges to see if 160.8 falls within aromatic range. Let's retrieve carbon shifts.
